transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. 

It's just... well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I'm sure it's probably just me, but... like, if I'm working and one saw starts up in the shop, or somebody just walks past the office, or even if I just have a passing thought about another job... it completely pulls me off what I’m doing. And then, I don't know, the whole day just sort of gets away from me. 

I feel awful about it, because I really do try to be a good worker, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you noticed this same problem with staying focused in other areas of your life, like at home, in conversations, or while doing everyday tasks?

Oh, um... I haven't really thought about it like that. I don't think so? I mean, I try very hard to be a good listener when people are talking to me, because I'd absolutely hate for anyone to think I was being rude or ignoring them. 

And at home, I just... well, I do my best to keep up with the chores and everything. I don't think it's a big problem there. It's mostly just at the shop where I feel like I'm really messing up and letting people down. I hope that's a helpful answer? I just haven't really noticed it with the everyday stuff, to be honest. Is it okay if it's mostly just happening at work?
Do you often feel restless or find yourself needing to be constantly moving, especially during situations where you’re expected to stay still, like during meetings or while working on a task?

Oh, um... I don't want you to think I'm running around disrupting things or being a bother, because I really do try my absolute best to be professional. But... well, I guess if I have to sit at the desk doing estimates, or if I have to sit through a really long meeting, I do get a little... uncomfortable? 

It's like I feel all wound up inside, like I just really need to get up and move around. I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish what I'm doing, and I really try to! Even though my wrist is completely healed up now and I don't have an excuse to stretch it, I still get that urge to just... get up. 

I feel a bit awful admitting that, because I know adults are supposed to be able to sit still and I don't want to seem like I'm acting like a child. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions right.

Outside of work, do you ever notice these same difficulties with staying focused or feeling restless in other situations, like when you're at home relaxing, running errands, or spending time with friends or family?

Oh, um... well, I really try my best to be respectful, especially in places where everyone is supposed to be quiet. I would absolutely hate to be a disruption to anyone. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, sometimes when things are very quiet, like at church, or even just sitting at home in the evening... I do catch myself doing it. 

I'll realize I'm tapping my foot, or shifting around in my seat a lot, or leaning over to whisper to my husband. Sometimes I even get up and walk to the back or go to the restroom for no real reason at all, just because sitting perfectly still in all that quiet feels almost... unbearable? 

I feel so guilty admitting that, especially about church, because I know a woman my age should just be able to sit peacefully like everyone else. I really do try to be good and just stay put, I promise. I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Looking back, did you have similar struggles with staying focused or feeling restless when you were a child, like in school or during family activities?

Oh, um... well, I really hate to speak poorly of myself as a child, because my mother tried so hard with me, and I wouldn't want you to think I was a bad kid or a troublemaker. I always wanted to be a good student! 

But... I suppose, if I think all the way back to grade school, even before I was 12... it was a bit of a struggle. My teachers were always telling my mother that I was a bright girl, which was very kind of them to say, but... they also said I was a bit careless. 

I'd lose my homework, or I'd forget the instructions they just gave us. And I guess I spent an awful lot of time just staring out the window when I was supposed to be doing my seatwork. I really didn't mean to be disobedient! It was just so hard to keep my mind on the paper. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was just lazy... I really did try to do what I was told. Is that what you meant by struggling when I was younger?

Can you tell me if these problems with staying focused and feeling restless happen in other places besides work and church, like when you're at home with your family, running errands, or spending time with friends?

Oh, um... well, I really hate to admit this because I don't want to sound like I'm not capable or that I'm not trying my hardest. I really do try so, so hard to be reliable for everyone. But... I guess it does spill over into other things, yes. 

At work, I've... well, I've made some little mistakes here and there. Sometimes it's meant we had to redo some work, or... or I've lost out on a commission because of delays. And I think the crew... I think they might be a little hesitant to trust me with the ordering or the schedule right now. I feel just terrible about it, because I never want to let my team down. 

And at home... oh, my poor husband. He's so patient with me, he really is. But he's had to take over paying the bills and keeping track of our reminders because I just... I kept misplacing the papers, or I'd completely forget what needed to be done until it was too late. I feel so awful putting that burden on him when I should be able to manage a simple household task. I know I should be doing better. Does that... does that answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
